description.value:
Frequency at will

Make two Strikes, one with each weapon (or your weapon and your Snapjaw's jaws, if it's adjacent), against a single target, committing both into one overlapping attack and trading accuracy for the chance both connect. Both use your current multiple attack penalty, but against your Marked quarry the second Strike's penalty is reduced by 1 (2 at Veteran tier or higher) — the go-to opener.

cinderfall.incomplete: This is Waywarden's own Double Slice analog. P8 (Double Slice) confirms that even the real, system-native "make two Strikes as one attack, combine damage" resolution is hardcoded engine behavior, not something system.rules reproduces — only a minor penalty flag is rule-element material, and the Mark-conditioned MAP discount on top of that is separately blocked. This hands the actor a wholly new usable action/reaction. Confirmed absent per two direct spot checks: Fighter's Double Slice only rule-encodes its minor non-agile penalty -- the actual "resolve two Strikes as one attack, combine damage" behavior is hardcoded PF2e system logic. Fighter's Reactive Strike is granted via a bare GrantItem whose trigger is likewise hardcoded system behavior tied to one specific compendium action UUID, not a generic rule-element hook. Any Waywarden card proposing an equivalent bespoke Strike-triggering or multi-Strike-resolving action inherits the same gap. The Waywarden's central subsystem, The Mark (classes.waywarden.json flags.cinderfall.terms[0]: "designate a creature as your quarry, gaining a growing bonus to track, target, and punish it specifically"), has zero Foundry-schema footprint anywhere in the corpus. classes.waywarden.json:65 itself carries "rules": []. No card anywhere grants a TokenMark effect (site/data/cards/abilities/, class-features/, feat-effects/ are all empty scaffold directories -- confirmed via ls, contents are .gitkeep only). Real pf2e's own equivalent mechanic (Ranger's Hunt Prey) is fully buildable and precedented, but that infrastructure (an action item + a TokenMark-carrying effect item) does not exist for Waywarden and is not one of the 56 files in scope for this draft. This card is blocked until a future pass authors the base Mark action/effect.
